# package mbcap

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-modbus-capture/mbcap"
```

Package mbcap reads and writes the MBCAP binary capture format (.mbcap) of docs/FORMAT.md section 2: a magic number followed by CRC32C-protected blocks. Samples refer to request templates, carry delta-coded times, and store each response raw, as "same as before" or as a sparse word diff against the previous response to the same request in the same block. Every data block is independently decodable and optionally deflate-compressed.

Writers never seek. A file cut short by a crash is readable up to its last complete block (the reader then returns an error wrapping capture.ErrTruncated); Repair rewrites it as a complete file.

## Constants

```go
const (
	// MaxBlockLen is the largest block payload a reader accepts.
	MaxBlockLen = 32 << 20
	// MaxBlockRaw is the largest uncompressed data block body.
	MaxBlockRaw = 16 << 20
	// MaxTemplates is the largest number of request templates.
	MaxTemplates = capture.MaxRequests
)
```

Limits for hostile input.

```go
const (
	DefaultBlockSamples = 256
	DefaultBlockBytes   = 64 << 10
)
```

Default block size limits.

```go
const FooterLen = 1 + 1 + 8 + 4 + 4
```

FooterLen is the size of the footer block: type, length, index offset, tag and CRC.

```go
const Magic = "\x89MBCAP\r\n"
```

Magic is the first 8 bytes of every MBCAP file.

## Variables

```go
var ErrNoFooter = errors.New("mbcap: no valid footer")
```

ErrNoFooter is returned by ReadIndex for a file without a valid footer, such as one cut short by a crash. Repair rewrites such a file.

### type Compression

```go

```

Compression selects how a Writer compresses data blocks.

```go
const (
	// Deflate compresses every data block with compress/flate (the default).
	Deflate Compression = iota
	// NoCompression stores data blocks uncompressed: for live capture, where
	// blocks are flushed often and should cost little CPU.
	NoCompression
)
```

Compressions. A block that deflate does not make smaller is stored uncompressed either way.

#### func ReadIndex

```go
func ReadIndex(r io.ReaderAt, size int64) (*Index, error)
```

ReadIndex reads the index of a complete file from its end, without reading the data blocks. It checks the footer and the index block's CRC, not the rest of the file.

### type Reader

```go
type Reader struct {

	// offset of the next byte to read

	// SkipCorrupt makes the reader skip a block whose CRC does not match,
	// instead of failing. Samples in a skipped data block are lost; a skipped
	// definition makes later samples fail. Set it before the first Next.
	SkipCorrupt bool

}
```

Reader reads an MBCAP file as a stream of records. It checks every block's CRC and every record against the model's invariants (capture.Checker), and at the end the index against the blocks it read.


RepairReport says what Repair kept.

#### func Repair

```go
func Repair(dst io.Writer, src io.Reader, opts *Options) (RepairReport, error)
```

Repair reads src as far as it can and writes a complete file to dst, with a new index and footer. It skips blocks with a bad CRC and stops at a truncation or any other error, keeping everything before it. The end is unknown unless src still holds its index. It fails only when the header cannot be read or dst cannot be written.

### type Writer

```go
type Writer struct {

	// offset of the next byte written

	// The open data block.

}
```

Writer writes an MBCAP file. It never seeks, so it can write to a pipe. Blocks are written as they fill; Flush ends the current one, so that the file is readable up to there.

#### func NewWriter

```go
func NewWriter(w io.Writer, h capture.Header, opts *Options) (*Writer, error)
```

NewWriter checks h and writes the magic number and the header block.

#### func (Writer) Close

```go
func (w *Writer) Close(end capture.End) error
```

Close ends the open data block, writes the index and footer, and flushes. Use capture.End{} when the end is unknown.

#### func (Writer) Flush

```go
func (w *Writer) Flush() error
```

Flush ends the open data block and flushes everything written to the underlying writer. The file is then readable up to here. A live recorder calls it on a timer.

#### func (Writer) WriteSample

```go
func (w *Writer) WriteSample(s capture.Sample) error
```

WriteSample adds a sample to the open data block, unless the capture does not store it (see capture.Writer). A request seen for the first time gets a template block first.

WriteStream writes a stream block.
